text: Most families in Pakistan build a house once. The plan goes back and forth with a draftsman for weeks, and nobody checks the bylaws until the authority sends it back.
Naqsha designs the home with them. Every agent in it runs on NVIDIA Nemotron, served by Nebius Token Factory.
This family has a ten marla plot in Islamabad. They describe it in one message, and a setup agent on Nemotron 3 Super fills in the brief.

Naqsha ships with Lahore's rules. For Islamabad, it searched the web with Tavily, found the CDA's own regulations, and Nemotron 3 Ultra turned them into a rule pack, with every number linked to its source.
A family that already has a drawing can upload a photo of it. Nemotron's vision model reads every room, and the design keeps their layout.
Four exteriors come back, and the family picks one.

Then the architect agent gets to work. Nemotron 3 Ultra drafts three floor plans at once, a rules engine scores them, and a fixer agent repairs the best one through tool calls, trying each edit against the rules before it keeps it.
It writes the 3D model as code, from a checklist of every feature in the chosen concept.
The vision model compares the model with the concept, and anything missing goes back to be rebuilt.
Photos come from the model itself: from the road, the corner, the garden and the air. Every angle shows the same house.
Then the family walks through it, room by room, before the first brick.
Nemotron does all of the thinking. Ultra plans, fixes and writes the code, Super runs the conversation, and the vision model reads drawings and checks the build.
Naqsha. Open source, built on Nemotron and Nebius.
